crop_profile.summary: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a globally important annual cereal grown on loamy to clay soils with pH 6.0-7.5. Optimal temperatures are 10-25 °C, rainfall 300-900 mm/year, and sunlight 6-10 h/day. It requires medium water and nitrogen, with critical moisture needs during flowering. Major producers include China, India, Russia, the United States, and France. Typical yields are 3 t/ha, reaching up to 7 t/ha under optimal management. Key diseases are Fusarium head blight, powdery mildew, and leaf rust; main pests include aphids, Hessian fly, and wheat midge. Integrated pest management, split nitrogen fertilization, and timely harvest ensure high quality grain.

recommendation.recommendation: Conduct a comprehensive field inspection and implement targeted disease and nutrient management for the wheat crop.
recommendation.justification: Satellite imagery shows critical vegetation health (NDVI ≈ 0.30) indicating possible disease or nutrient deficiency, while soil health is excellent and weather conditions are favorable. Immediate scouting and corrective actions are needed to prevent yield loss and capitalize on the current soil and water opportunities.
actions: Walk the entire field and visually scout for symptoms of Fusarium head blight (bleached, shriveled kernels, pinkish heads) and powdery mildew (white powdery patches).
Collect suspect leaf and head samples and send to a diagnostic lab for pathogen confirmation.
Take soil and plant tissue samples for NPK and micronutrient analysis.
If Fusarium head blight is confirmed, apply a registered triazole fungicide at the flowering stage as per label rates.
If powdery mildew is detected, apply a sulfur‑based fungicide or appropriate systemic product.
Based on nutrient test results, adjust nitrogen fertilization (e.g., split application of 50 kg N ha⁻¹ now and the remainder during early grain fill).
Maintain the recommended irrigation schedule (surface or sprinkler, every 7‑10 days) to keep soil moisture adequate during flowering.
Record all observations, treatments, and application dates in a field log.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Early detection and treatment will restore vegetation health, mitigate disease spread, optimize nutrient status, and preserve expected wheat yield and profitability for the June‑August harvest.
monitoring_plan: Perform visual scouting every 3 days until disease symptoms are resolved.
Re‑run NDVI analysis via satellite or drone weekly to track canopy recovery (target NDVI ≥ 0.65).
Monitor soil moisture daily with field sensors to ensure irrigation adequacy.
Re‑test leaf tissue 10‑14 days after treatment to verify disease control and nutrient balance.
Update the field log with all observations and adjust management actions as needed.
